The DPW director's request for a second front-end loader ranked below the midpoint of the 35 ranked requests, and the ranking was not changed.

Asked how in-depth the Turkey Hill renovations will be and whether they would disturb the new entrance and cameras.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager recommended six items, including a rescue vehicle, school and Turkey Hill security and door upgrades, and dump trucks with spreaders.
No free cash is in the plan yet because state aid is unknown and the budget is level funded from the prior year; three items qualify for the special purpose stabilization fund.
Only the ambulance and two large dump trucks qualify for the fund, so ARPA funding for the rescue would not change the recommendation.
The accountant said stabilization balances meet thresholds but she prefers to keep the minimum OPEB contribution; capital depends on state aid.
The next items on the list are sizable, together more than half a million dollars.
Earmarks are usually no more than a set amount; a March 7 meeting with the legislative team was mentioned.
A member noted small engineering amounts for multi-year projects were pushed higher in priority.
Using ARPA for the ambulance would not push other items down the list; members debated whether special purpose stabilization funds suit plow trucks.
A member estimated abatement exposure from application counts and an assumed average abatement, and the overlay is usually in the low hundreds of thousands.

decisions.decision: A written narrative of the committee's work, plus the chart showing the manager's and committee's priorities, will be provided for the town meeting report; the chair pre-writes it without a further meeting.
No commitment on ARPA funding until the select board votes the following week.
